record.tranche_reason: Tests whether learned mappings between latent spaces can support cross-modal tasks, and whether alignment outcomes vary with the alignment cost and data available. It uses conditional flow matching and optimal-transport alignment rather than measuring convergence through the original sources’ methods.
record.gate_note: The study reports downstream mapping performance, coupling matching accuracy, and mapping error. It does not measure whether independently trained models’ unmodified representations become more alike as model scale or capability increases. The reported alignment is trained using paired examples or a coupling built from them.
record.test_reason: This is a methods paper. It trains a large conditional flow-matching model (adaLN-Large velocity field, about 49M parameters) with paired anchors to map one pre-trained latent space onto another. It then reports how well its own variants (true, global, local alignment; bridge vs KNN/KCCA costs) perform against baselines. It never measures whether independently trained models' representations converge, with scale or otherwise. The map is neither simple nor linear, and it is trained with labelled pairs, so the downstream accuracies show what this heavy learned method can do, not that the spaces are interchangeable as V4 states. The cost and solver comparisons concern OT coupling quality, not the convergence similarity measures V6 is about. Mapping networks to monkey V4/IT activity is model-to-brain, not model-to-model.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that the bridge cost enables effective cross-modal mapping with limited pairs, and that global alignment is competitive and overfits less than true alignment in noisy settings. They add that mapping quality depends on intra-space separation and inter-space alignment, and is limited by feature-extractor quality and pair availability. The abstract also claims it matches end-to-end trained models when labelled data is scarce (under 20%). They make no claim about representations converging.
record.recipe_differences: Uses conditional flow matching with true or optimal-transport-based alignment and reports downstream task performance; it does not reproduce the original sources’ convergence measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with alignment strategy (true, global, local), OT solver and cost function, paired-data proportion, and feature-space overlap.

fits_no_version.finding: A conditional flow trained with about 10% paired anchors maps ViT-B image features into MiniLM text space, with class-retrieval accuracy the text calls comparable to ViT's 83.97 classifier head (figure only).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pre-trained vision and text encoder spaces can be bridged by a learned nonlinear generative map using few paired anchors, at near classifier-level class decoding.

fits_no_version.finding: The bridge cost, built from intra-space distances plus paired anchors, gives higher OT coupling matching accuracy than KNN or KCCA costs, and accuracy rises with the number of pairs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Intra-space geometry plus a few anchors suffices to recover cross-modal correspondences, and recovery improves with more anchors.

fits_no_version.finding: Mapping quality falls as within-model class overlap in the source space rises (MNIST and ImageNet).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cross-space mapping quality depends on how well separated the source model's features are.

fits_no_version.finding: Flows from six vision networks to monkey IT and V4 activity: MSE rises with more pairs under true alignment and falls under global alignment. MSE-based model ranking is not consistent with Brain-Score, while downstream accuracy roughly is.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Model-to-brain alignment quality depends on the alignment strategy used.

record.problems: The study evaluates learned mappings rather than spontaneous representation convergence. Many relevant outcomes are presented only in figures, with no numerical values or uncertainty estimates in the text. The artificial-to-neural MSE trend is stated in aggregate, while individual model and layer results are plotted.
record.rows_left_out: The supplementary layer-by-layer mappings and downstream classification curves for individual artificial networks and regions (Figures 21–24) are not separately itemized; the main-text aggregate trends for these settings are recorded in r21–r24.

untested.parts: All of it: no scale or capability sweep and no cross-model similarity measurement.
All of it: there is one image model and one text model, and their inherent alignment is never measured or related to model quality.
All of it: no comparison across seeds.
Simple or linear maps, stitching, relative representations, mapping without paired data, and loss relative to an unmapped native model. Only a heavy learned flow trained with pairs is evaluated.
All of it: no feature or circuit analysis.
All of it: no convergence similarity metric is varied. The OT cost comparisons concern coupling quality for the study's own method.
All of it: no measure of alignment level, plateau, or its causes.

record.verdict_notes: The reader marked V4 and V6 as tested, but both links fail. For V4, the map is a large generative flow trained with pairs, and the evaluation compares the study's own methods. For V6, the cost comparisons are about OT coupling for the method, not convergence metrics. All rows are relinked to none, and no verdicts are given. Most values are figure-only, with no uncertainty reported despite 5 seeds. The study cites the Platonic Representation Hypothesis only as motivation.

versions.untested_parts: No scale or capability sweep, and no test of convergence among independently trained models as they grow.
The image-text experiment uses paired image and text representations, but does not test whether their inherent alignment increases as both models improve.
No comparison of training seeds or shared features across same-architecture networks.
Tests learned conditional-flow mappings trained with paired data; does not test linear maps, stitching, relative representations, or alignment without paired data.
No recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits are identified across models.
Tests variation across OT cost functions, paired-data amounts, and feature-space overlap, but not different numbers of neighbours for a convergence metric or out-of-distribution inputs.
Does not test whether convergence plateaus or whether shared training data or objectives explain it.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: ImageNet at approximately 10% paired data, and MNIST image-to-text and text-to-image tasks
reader_labels.reason: The learned mappings reached classifier-comparable ImageNet performance at approximately 10% paired data and performed on par with or better than MNIST baselines in the reported settings (r2, r4-r7).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: ImageNet with very few paired samples or local alignment; artificial-to-neural mappings with true alignment
reader_labels.reason: ImageNet global alignment performed poorly with very few pairs, local alignment failed to converge, and true alignment to neural data showed increasing MSE as paired data increased (r1, r3, r21, r23).
